interactions.summary: Jiang compares Dante's late-life condition to Jesus facing crucifixion and Moses barred from the Promised Land, then uses those analogies to argue that the final cantos are Dante's courageous testament of faith, hope, and love.
A student asks whether Jiang calls hope arrogance because hoping is inherently centered in the first-person self.

claims.claim: Jiang says the lowest point of Dante's life is best understood through analogies to Jesus awaiting crucifixion and Moses seeing but not entering the Promised Land.
He argues that Dante's courage lies in embracing faith, hope, and love when he has no evidence that the Divine Comedy will ever change the world.
Jiang presents the last ten cantos as Dante's will and testament to humanity and says their full meaning has not yet been adequately revealed.
He gives the class three rules for the next two sessions: stay focused on revealing Dante's message, participate fully, and act with faith, hope, and love rather than with ego, fear, and doubt.
Jiang says faith is ultimately an act of imagination, and he contrasts Paul saying there is a plan with Dante saying that we are the plan.
He defines hope as arrogance, meaning the conviction that one can help change the world rather than waiting humbly for God to do it alone.

signature_moments.moment: The final ten cantos are cast as Dante's will and testament to humanity, written at the edge of death and despair.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Dante's will and testament to humanity
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's central framing move for why the end of Paradiso should be read as a civilizational bequest rather than as merely doctrinal poetry.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang flips Paul into Dante by saying not merely that there is a plan, but that we are the plan.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns faith from passive compliance into participatory imagination and anchors the lecture's broader human-agency thesis.

signature_moments.moment: Hope is defined not as humility but as arrogance.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of Jiang's sharpest reinterpretations of a theological virtue and becomes a governing concept for the rest of the class.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's triad for reading the final cantos, where faith is imagination, hope is world-changing arrogance, and love will complete the interpretive arc.
Jiang's shorthand for Dante's participatory theology: human imagination helps animate divine reality rather than merely submitting to it.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang ties Dante's 1321 endpoint to the class's present 2026 mission, treating this session as a delayed unveiling of what Dante meant for humanity.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang's offhand dating and location phrasing include minor ASR noise, but the core point is the present class as a belated revelation of Dante's final intention.
